method: Reviewed the complete delivery lesson, its output-generating Python fence, checkpoint claims, referenced synthetic approval sample, and the dated clean-run narrative. Test-first checks caught an overclaim: a 0.03-second script process duration was used to attribute all handoff cost to locating the script, although path-discovery time was not separately measured. Narrowed the conclusion to the observed missing working directory and explicitly separated measured script runtime from unmeasured handoff time. Executed the handoff template offline; no provider or network call was made.

observations.trace: The static template executes and prints all six sections. The six-block order is explicitly adaptable; logging guidance requires data minimization; the 7-step approval comparison is limited to a synthetic sample and not a production rule. The clean-run narrative now says the first command failed because the working directory was omitted, while the recorded 0.03 s measures only the script process; time spent discovering the path was not measured, so total handoff cost cannot be attributed to it. Preserved ERR-055 verifier passes 7/7.

limitations: The 0.03-second value remains a dated historical observation and was not independently reproduced from its original environment or raw timing trace.
The static template does not collect project facts, run a clean-checkout handoff, validate production telemetry, or prove independent handoff readiness.
The approval comparison remains synthetic and does not establish a universal approval policy.
